articles.title: Bag stolen from reserved train coach; Railway loses appeal against Rs 1.45 lakh payout to passenger
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Delhi state consumer commission has upheld an order directing Northern Railway to pay Rs 1.45 lakh to a passenger whose bag was stolen from
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Delhi state consumer commission has upheld an order directing Northern Railway to pay Rs 1.45 lakh to a passenger whose bag was stolen from a reserved train coach. The commission said the railway could not avoid responsibility by arguing that the passenger's luggage's are not covered under tickets, as the theft involved unauthorised persons entering a reserved compartment.The commission also noted that railway staff failed to prevent the intrusion and did not properly help the passenger lodge an FIR. It dismissed Northern Railway's appeal on October 6, 2026, upholding the district commission's order.BackgroundAs per the commission order, Ajoy Kumar was travelling from Delhi to Patna on Mahananda Express on June 7, 2014, when two unauthorised persons entered his reserved coach and stole his trolley bag.The bag allegedly contained jewellery, clothes and other belongings worth Rs 1.2 lakh. Kumar alleged that he immediately approached the TTE in coach and asked for an FIR to be lodged.However, the FIR was registered only on April 23, 2015. The complainant continued to follow up with the railway authorities and later learnt that the case had been marked as untraced in May 2017. He then approached the consumer commission, seeking compensation for the loss.Northern Railway denied responsibility, arguing that the luggage had not been booked with it and was in the passenger's personal custody. It also relied on Section 100 of the Railways Act, which limits the railway's responsibility for luggage unless negligence by railway staff is established. It further argued that the matter involved theft and should be dealt with under criminal law.The district consumer commission ruled in Kumar's favour on April 16, 2024, directing Northern Railway to pay Rs 1.2 lakh with 9 percent annual interest from September 7, 2017, and Rs 25,000 as compensation. The railway challenged that order before the state commission.Why did the commission hold the railway responsible?A bench of President Justice Sangita Dhingra Sehgal and member Bimla Kumari noted that the district commission was right in holding the railway liable for negligence and deficiency in service.The bench said the issue was not simply whether the passenger had kept his luggage in his own custody. It was whether the railway had taken reasonable steps to stop unauthorised people from entering a reserved coach.“A passenger who purchases a reserved ticket is entitled to a reasonable assurance of safety and security of his personal safety and belongings,” the commission observed.It said allowing unauthorised persons to enter a reserved compartment went against the railway's duty towards passengers. The commission also noted that the railway had not produced records such as the TTE's duty roster, staff deployment details or other material explaining how the intruders gained access to the coach.The bench said the railway could not escape liability merely because the stolen items had not been formally booked. What mattered was whether negligence by railway staff had contributed to the loss.“The liability of the Appellant does not arise merely because a theft occurred, but because the theft was made possible due to the admitted failure of the railway staff to prevent unauthorized intrusion into a reserved compartment,” the order said.The commission also took note of the passenger's efforts to report the theft. It said he had approached the TTE soon after the incident, but the railway failed to lodge the FIR promptly. Later, a railway communication stated that the status had been conveyed to him by phone, but the number mentioned in the letter did not belong to him.The bench said the railway had not explained where its staff were or what steps had been taken to prevent unauthorised entry.“The Appellant cannot be permitted to take advantage of a lapses which are entirely of its own making,” the commission said.It concluded that the district commission had correctly found deficiency in service and dismissed Northern Railway's appeal, with no order as to costs.What did the commission order?The Delhi State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, in its October 6, 2026 order, upheld the district commission's directions requiring Northern Railway to:Pay Rs 1.2 lakh to Ajoy Kumar, with 9 percent annual interest from September 7, 2017, until payment.Pay Rs 25,000 as compensation for mental pain, agony and harassment.Make the payment within 30 days of the district commission's order.The district commission had also directed that, if payment was not made within 30 days, the railway would have to pay 12 percent annual interest on the entire awarded amount from the expiry of that period.

articles.title: 'I may share it with Trump': Navi Pillay jokes after winning the Nobel Peace Prize
articles.summary: Navi Pillay, the South African jurist who won the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize, joked about sharing the honour with US President Donald Trump while reacting to
articles.body: Navi Pillay, the South African jurist who won the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize, joked about sharing the honour with US President Donald Trump while reacting to the announcement, bringing renewed attention to the Republican leader’s deep desire to receive the prestigious award.“If you clap a little bit more I may share this prize with Trump,” Pillay said in Nuremberg after being applauded following news of her win. She was recognised for her efforts to promote peace and international law by ensuring that war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide are prosecuted.Trump & his 'Nobel' quest Trump has repeatedly expressed his desire to win the Nobel Peace Prize and has argued that his diplomatic efforts deserve recognition. His pursuit of the award drew eyeballs in January this year, when Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado offered to share her 2025 prize with him.After Machado indicated that she wanted to give him the award, Trump told Fox News that accepting it would be a “great honour”. The White House also said he deserved the Nobel Peace Prize “many times over” after the award's organisers ruled that it could not be transferred to another person.Machado won the 2025 Nobel Peace Prize for promoting democratic rights and campaigning for a peaceful transition from dictatorship to democracy. The Nobel Committee described her as one of Latin America's most extraordinary examples of civilian courage in recent times.She was elected to Venezuela's National Assembly in 2010 but was removed from office in 2014. Ahead of the 2024 presidential election, she won the opposition primary but was barred from contesting. She subsequently backed Edmundo González Urrutia, whose supporters published voting records they said showed he had defeated President Nicolás Maduro. Maduro's government claimed victory and intensified its crackdown on opponents.Machado was living in hiding when she won the award, and her daughter, Ana Corina Sosa, accepted the medal and diploma on her behalf at the December 2025 ceremony in Oslo.On January 15, 2026, Machado presented her Nobel Peace Prize medal to Trump during a meeting at the White House, saying the gesture recognised his commitment to Venezuela's freedom. Trump thanked her publicly and called it a “wonderful gesture of mutual respect”.However, the Norwegian Nobel Institute clarified that although the physical medal could change hands, the Nobel Peace Prize itself could not be shared or transferred. The title of laureate remains with the person or organisation selected by the committee.All about Navanethem PillayPillay, whose full name is Navanethem Pillay, was born in Durban during apartheid into a family of Indian Tamil origin. She became a pioneering lawyer and jurist, serving on South Africa's high court before joining the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda.She later served at the International Criminal Court and as the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights. She also chaired the UN commission of inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory and is currently a judge at the International Court of Justice, which is hearing a case concerning allegations of genocide against Myanmar.Pillay played a significant role in landmark rulings recognising rape and sexual violence as possible acts of genocide and crimes against humanity. She was also involved in cases examining how media propaganda can incite hatred and violence against targeted communities.The Nobel Committee said her work demonstrated the importance of international law in resolving conflicts peacefully, holding powerful states and individuals accountable, and protecting victims. It also highlighted concerns about the weakening of international legal institutions and the growing influence of power politics over the rule of law.Previous Nobel Peace Prize winnersIn 2024, the Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to Nihon Hidankyo, a Japanese grassroots organisation representing survivors of the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki.The organisation was recognised for its efforts to achieve a world free of nuclear weapons and for using survivors' testimonies to demonstrate why nuclear weapons must never be used again.The awards to Nihon Hidankyo, Machado and Pillay have recognised different approaches to peace, ranging from nuclear disarmament and democratic rights to accountability for war crimes and genocide.You use AI every day. articles.title: Denise Richards became a Hollywood face for shelter dogs, introducing rescued animals through Best Friends' adoption campaign
articles.summary: Actress Denise Richards used her Hollywood profile to promote shelter animal adoption through a monthly television segment launched in partnership with
articles.body: Actress Denise Richards used her Hollywood profile to promote shelter animal adoption through a monthly television segment launched in partnership with Best Friends Animal Society and Access Hollywood Live in February 2011. The initiative introduced viewers to rescued animals looking for permanent homes, beginning with Rascal, a tan Chihuahua rescued in the Los Angeles area. Richards, a longtime supporter and ambassador for Best Friends, helped bring attention to animals that needed adopters. Her involvement extended beyond television appearances: she also adopted a blind dog named Preston through the organisation. The effort combined celebrity visibility with a practical goal, encouraging viewers to consider adopting pets from shelters and rescue groups.How Denise Richards helped promote shelter dog adoptionBest Friends Animal Society announced the television segment on February 24, 2011. The monthly feature on Access Hollywood Live was designed to introduce an adoptable animal to viewers and provide information for people interested in offering a pet a permanent home.Richards introduced the first featured dog, Rascal, a tan Chihuahua rescued in the Los Angeles area. At the time, the dog was available for adoption. Viewers interested in Rascal or other animals could contact Best Friends for information about adoption opportunities.The initiative gave shelter animals exposure beyond the people who visited adoption centres. By presenting individual pets on a television programme, the segment allowed viewers to learn about animals that might otherwise have received less public attention.Why Best Friends Animal Society launched the segmentBest Friends Animal Society is a nonprofit organisation working with shelters, rescue groups and communities to find homes for homeless pets. Its programmes include animal care, adoption initiatives and partnerships intended to improve outcomes for dogs and cats in shelters.The television segment formed part of those broader efforts. Best Friends partnered with Access Hollywood Live to introduce adoptable animals to a wider audience and encourage people to consider bringing a shelter pet into their homes.The format focused on individual animals rather than adoption in the abstract. Viewers could see a particular dog, learn that it needed a home and find out how to enquire about adopting it. The organisation hoped that the additional exposure would help more animals find permanent homes.Richards also adopted a blind dog named PrestonRichards’ involvement with animal welfare was not limited to promoting adoption on television. In May 2011, Fox News reported that she had adopted a blind dog named Preston through Best Friends Animal Society.Richards said she contacted the organisation after her mother’s dog, Sheena, died. She wanted to adopt an animal that might be harder to place, and eventually brought Preston home.Her decision offered a personal example of adopting an animal with additional needs. It also reflected the message behind her public involvement: pets that may require extra care can still become companions in suitable homes.Preston’s adoption was separate from the television segment featuring Rascal. The two stories nevertheless show different aspects of Richards’ work with Best Friends, from encouraging viewers to adopt shelter animals to adopting a dog herself.Television exposure helped other shelter animals find homesIn a follow-up article published on February 15, 2012, Best Friends reported that dogs and cats from its Los Angeles programmes were regularly appearing on television, including on Access Hollywood and FOX’s Good Day LA. The organisation’s mobile adoption coordinator, Jf Pryor, said many animals found homes after appearing on television, with some adoption enquiries arriving as soon as the following day.The report described several successful adoptions. A German shepherd and Shiba Inu mix initially named Clarice was adopted and renamed Kazi. A six-year-old Yorkshire terrier mix called Lou Who, who had been found wandering alone, was adopted by viewers who saw her on television and renamed Lulu.Another dog, Ribbon, was featured on Good Day LA and reportedly had a suitable home lined up shortly afterwards. These cases demonstrate how television exposure can connect shelter animals with prospective adopters. The report did not establish that these particular adoptions resulted from Richards’ appearances specifically.The initiative was part of a wider effort involving animal welfare organisations, shelters, volunteers and prospective adopters. Although the available reports do not provide a total number of adoptions directly attributable to Richards’ segment, they document the programme’s purpose and describe how television appearances helped other shelter animals attract potential homes.You use AI every day. articles.title: An Ohio couple with no engineering background spent three weeks and $700 building a 12-foot-high backyard roller coaster for their two children; a video of the homemade 12-second ride later went viral
articles.summary: Some become parents by choice, and such parents give their children the best lives possible.
articles.body: Some become parents by choice, and such parents give their children the best lives possible. How else would you describe an Ohio couple who built a roller coaster in their backyard for their kids?Jon and Natasha Cain of Lancaster, Ohio, spent a few weekends and $700 on something their kids would remember for years: a roller coaster in the backyard, according to a report by ABC News. They had no engineering training but had the willpower to teach themselves the basics of how a roller coaster works.A summer projectMost kids would spend their summer holidays at a theme park. But often, the thrill of a ride is accompanied by a long queue. In the summer of 2009, the Cains took on the project of building a roller coaster. They used readily available materials that one could pick up at a local store: wood, concrete and PVC pipes. They put it together for their two children, daughter Olyvia and son Samual.The finished track rises 12 feet at its highest point and winds through a series of twists and turns. They worked on the roller coaster for three weeks and spent $700. But building a ride was not simple. It had to hold a child, negotiate tight curves and remain upright throughout every ride.Learning on the jobThe Cains weren’t engineers. The couple ran a car dealership, but they both enjoyed making things with their hands. They are the kind of people who cannot say no to a good DIY project. That was enough for them to get started on the roller coaster. The couple began by planning the layout. They went to a local store and bought the supplies they needed. The plan was to work out the rest as the project progressed.They thought the whole thing could be built for about $300. But when the final bill came, it was more than double the estimated cost: $700. Yet it was worth every single penny. Their kids could enjoy a ride without leaving the yard.Olyvia was only three when the roller coaster was built, and she was unsure at first. “My daughter was three when we built it and she loved it. At first, she was hesitant, but not scared,” Natasha said.Before building the roller coaster, the Cains also checked with local officials. Rather than shutting them down, the city encouraged the project. Jon later recalled receiving a simple go-ahead from officials.Once the roller coaster was complete, the Cains also filmed their children enjoying the ride. They uploaded the video to YouTube, and it went viral. The video showed Jon pushing Samual through the 12-second run, with the boy squealing with joy.After successfully completing their DIY roller coaster, the couple moved on to their next project. They wanted to build a log cabin. But their DIY adventures didn’t end there. “We did talk about doing a Ferris wheel at the new house … not like a ginormous one, just one that you could manually do,” Natasha added.You use AI every day. articles.title: Jeff Bridges felt guilty after learning the scale of global hunger in the 1980s; he joined Hollywood stars to raise $176,000 through an anti-hunger television special

articles.body: In January 1985, as critics debated whether Starman would make Jeff Bridges a star, the 35-year-old actor gave a breakfast interview to the Los Angeles Times to discuss world hunger. In the interview with the Los Angeles Times, He told reporter Deborah Caulfield that learning how many people die of starvation left him feeling tremendously guilty, since he enjoyed eating in nice restaurants and living in a nice home. He had been involved with the End Hunger Network for six years and had organised a benefit screening of the film. With other entertainers, he helped produce a television special that raised $176,000 with plans to air it in 50 more cities.How did Jeff Bridges help launch a global anti-hunger movementBridges had been involved with the End Hunger Network for six years and had recently organised a screening of Starman to benefit it. He told the paper he became involved when he learned about the immensity of the problem. He identified two facts in particular. The first was that the number of people who died at Hiroshima dies of starvation every three days. The second was that more people die in five years from hunger and related diseases than in all the wars, revolutions and murders of the previous 150 years.Bridges said the most impressive fact was that hunger did not have to continue. He attributed this view to both conservative and liberal experts, who say there is plenty of food and technology available. He added that these resources had already ended hunger in about 40 countries since the Second World War. The figures in this section are Bridges's own statements.How did Bridges bring Hollywood stars together to fight global hungerThis left Bridges feeling "tremendously guilty". He told the Times that he first felt he had to make some kind of giant, sacrificial gesture that he was not willing to make. He explained his reluctance in personal terms, saying that he liked eating in nice restaurants, flying first-class and living in a nice home.Rather than dwelling on that guilt, Bridges worked with friends to form an entertainment-industry contingent focused on world hunger. The article names Bud Cort, Dennis Weaver and Valerie Harper among them, along with his brother Beau and others. Bridges also linked the cause to his latest film, saying that in a way it was what Starman was about: that humanity is often at its best when things are at their worst, though people can become too calloused to see their own beauty.How did Bridges’ anti-hunger television special raise $176,000In the year before the interview, the group produced a show on the subject of hunger. The programme was hosted by Burt Lancaster, Gregory Peck and Jack Lemmon. When it aired in Los Angeles, the article states, it raised $176,000.The article adds that Bridges said plans were under way to air the special in 50 more cities in 1985. The same piece shows that his work on the issue ran alongside his film career, with the Starman benefit screening, the television special, and the upcoming Jagged Edge all discussed in the same interview. Bridges was searching for a project that could star the Bridges family, including his father Lloyd and his two brothers.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A UK founder and his mother burned through £15,000 developing a vegan supplement, then fitted kitchens to fund their first stock; Free Soul now turns over £55 million a year and employs 50
articles.summary: A mother and son in the UK who ran out of their £15,000 savings while developing a vegan protein supplement started fitting kitchens and installing
articles.body: A mother and son in the UK who ran out of their £15,000 savings while developing a vegan protein supplement started fitting kitchens and installing cupboards to raise money for their first stock. What began as a small business funded through their own savings has now grown into Free Soul, a supplements company with an annual turnover of £55 million and 50 employees.Arjun Sofat, a former analyst at an investment bank, started the company with his mother, Rohini Sofat, in 2017, according to a report by The Standard. The two initially spent £15,000 developing and improving the formula for their first vegan protein product. When the money ran out, they decided to take up renovation work rather than seek early investment from outside investors.The pair continued fitting kitchens and installing cupboards until they had saved enough to purchase their first pallet of supplements. Nearly a decade after its launch, the company's products are now sold through major UK retailers.The company has also expanded beyond its original vegan protein supplement. Its range now includes protein powders, electrolyte powders, hair and skin gummies, and other nutritional supplements. Despite the company's growth, Sofat believes that starting with limited money helped him understand customers and build the business without depending on early venture capital funding.Rohini's health struggles inspired Free SoulThe idea for Free Soul came from Rohini's personal experience with health and fitness. She was going through extreme stress because of her husband's illness and had started exercising heavily to cope with the situation.Her routine included attending Barry's Bootcamp classes, but despite the exercise, she continued to feel "awful". She then began exploring nutritional supplements, only to find that many products marketed towards women focused on weight loss rather than strength and overall wellbeing.Arjun told The Standard, “but the industry seemed obsessed with helping women get smaller. We thought the conversation should be about helping women feel stronger,”At the time, Arjun was working at an investment bank, where he dealt with mergers and acquisitions involving consumer health businesses. His professional experience exposed him to large companies operating in the same industry that he and his mother were beginning to explore.However, he found himself increasingly interested in developing a product that addressed the problem they had identified.He recalled, “and I realised I was spending my days analysing billion-pound businesses while thinking far more about solving this problem. So, I left banking to start the company with my mum.”Developing their first supplementNeither Arjun nor Rohini began with a large team or an established product development operation. Instead, they contacted nutritionists directly to understand ingredients and work on the formulation of their vegan protein supplement.They also had to learn how to build and operate an online business. The two used YouTube tutorials to teach themselves website design and how to create Amazon product listings.Arjun described this process as “YouTube University”. They would pause instructional videos, follow the steps and build their own versions of what was being demonstrated.The initial £15,000 came from Arjun's savings from his investment banking salary. Much of it went into developing the product before they had enough stock to begin selling.With their savings exhausted, the mother and son started a renovation business. The money earned from installing kitchens and cupboards eventually allowed them to purchase their first batch of products.Finding the first customersAfter launching the company in 2017, Arjun and Rohini focused on introducing their products directly to potential customers.They regularly woke up at 4am and drove around London, visiting gyms and handing out free samples to people exercising there. On one occasion, Arjun spotted singer Harry Styles lifting weights and approached him to talk about the brand.Alongside these visits, Arjun managed the company's social media accounts himself. Without a dedicated marketing budget, he worked on building an online audience and eventually attracted 13,000 followers.He explained, “When you don’t have a marketing budget, you have to replace money with energy. You say yes to everything, you meet everyone and do lots of things that don’t scale.”Rather than raising money from investors during its early years, the company relied on the founders' savings and revenue generated from product sales. The money earned was reinvested into the business.Reflecting on those years, Arjun said, “Having no money was probably an advantage,” adding, “It forced us to stay close to our customers.”From £15,000 savings to £55 million turnoverFree Soul's growth was initially gradual, but a viral moment on TikTok Shop helped accelerate sales. The company's expanding product range also contributed to its growth. The company recorded turnover exceeding £35 million last year, alongside a pre-tax profit of £5.5 million. Its annual turnover has now reached £55 million, and the company employs 50 people.Arjun acknowledges competition from larger supplement companies but believes that established relationships with customers provide an advantage. He said competitors might reproduce individual products, but they cannot easily replicate "years of customer relationships and the culture behind a brand".The next goal is to build the company into a £100 million business. However, Arjun is not planning to rush into international markets. He believes the company still has considerable room to grow within the UK and that expanding overseas too early could divert attention from existing opportunities.“Everyone asks if we’re going international, but I actually think founders can become distracted by expansion. We still see an enormous opportunity in the UK,” he said.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: West Bengal bypolls: BJP sweeps Nandigram, breaks through in Muslim-majority Rejinagar; PM Modi hails win
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Friday won both Nandigram and Rejinagar in West Bengal's assembly bypolls.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Friday won both Nandigram and Rejinagar in West Bengal's assembly bypolls. The result is particularly significant as it comes months after the saffron party won a thumping majority in West Bengal, ending Trinamool Congress's 15-year rule.In Nandigram, BJP candidate Hasi Rani Rath polled 1,64,427 votes to defeat Congress candidate Milan Pradhan, who secured 41,674 votes. Rath is the mother of Chandranath Rath, former personal assistant of chief minister Suvendu Adhikari, who was shot dead in May.In Rejinagar, BJP candidate Shankharavh Sarkar won with 1,29,914 votes. His nearest rival, Aam Janata Unnayan Party (AJUP) candidate Golam Nabi Azad, secured 54,098 votes. The BJP’s victory is particularly noteworthy given that Muslims account for nearly 70% of the voters in the constituency.Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated BJP on its victories in the Nandigram and Rejinagar assembly bypolls in West Bengal and the Nagaon Lok Sabha bypoll in Assam. He said the results reflected people's deep-rooted connection with the BJP-NDA's good governance agenda.In a post on X, PM Modi wrote, "Gratitude to the people for their continuous blessings! The Lok Sabha result of Nagaon (Assam) and Assembly results of Nandigram as well as Rejinagar (West Bengal) show yet again that the people have a deep-rooted connect with the good governance agenda of BJP-NDA. I congratulate the victorious BJP candidates and also applaud the hardwork of our Party Karyakartas. I also congratulate our valued NDA ally, the AINRC, for their win in Thattanchavady in Puducherry. This mandate will give us added strength as we work tirelessly for the welfare of the people and to fulfil their aspirations for a brighter and more prosperous future," PM Modi said.Nandigram: Mamata's former bastionHasi Rani Rath's victory consolidates the BJP's position in Nandigram, in Purba Medinipur district. The constituency has remained central to West Bengal's political narrative since the anti-land acquisition movement helped propel the Trinamool Congress to power in 2011.Nandigram later became the site of a high-profile contest between Adhikari and Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee in the 2021 assembly elections. Suvendu defeated Mamata in that election.Rath's candidature also carried an emotional dimension. Her son, Chandranath Rath, was shot dead by gunmen in Madhyamgram, on the outskirts of Kolkata, on May 6. The killing took place two days after the BJP won the West Bengal assembly elections.The bypoll was necessitated after Adhikari, who won Nandigram in the 2026 assembly elections, retained Bhabanipur.The opposition failed to mount a serious challenge to Rath. CPI candidate Santi Gopal Giri finished third with 5,779 votes. Other candidates, including those from the Left Front, ISF and the rebel Trinamool faction, Democratic Trinamool Congress, lost their deposits.The opposition camp suffered a setback on September 18 when TMC candidate Sanchita Pradhan Dey, a schoolteacher, withdrew her nomination after meeting Adhikari with her husband. Mamata Banerjee’s faction then extended last-minute support to Congress candidate Milan Pradhan under the INDIA alliance.However, police arrested Pradhan barely an hour later over pending warrants in four murder cases linked to the 2007 land acquisition movement. He secured interim bail from the Calcutta high court and resumed campaigning.READ ALSO:'Anti-monopoly, not anti-business': Rahul Gandhi demands 'level playing field' for corporationsRejinagar: BJP wins Muslim-majority seatSarkar's victory in Rejinagar, in Murshidabad district, marks a breakthrough for the BJP in a constituency that has traditionally seen contests involving the Trinamool Congress, Congress and regional parties.Sarkar won by 75,816 votes, polling 1,29,914 votes against Azad's 54,098. Congress candidate Abdullahil Kafi received 6,168 votes, while Mamata faction's nominee Rabiul Alam Chowdhury polled 3,847. The CPI(M)'s Md Sayeed secured 3,797 votes, and Democratic Trinamool Congress candidate Safiuzzaman Saikh received 2,044.The fragmented opposition failed to mount a competitive challenge, leaving the BJP well ahead of its rivals.The bypoll was necessitated after AJUP founder Humayun Kabir vacated Rejinagar. A former Trinamool Congress leader, Kabir later founded the AJUP and won the constituency by more than 58,000 votes in the 2026 assembly elections. He retained Nowda, prompting the bypoll. His son, Golam Nabi Azad, contested this time on the AJUP ticket.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: TN bypolls: Ruling TVK wins first test, but vettri not impressive
articles.summary: CHENNAI: Chief minister C Joseph Vijay-led Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) cleared its first electoral test barely five months after forming a govt in
articles.body: CHENNAI: Chief minister C Joseph Vijay-led Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) cleared its first electoral test barely five months after forming a govt in Tamil Nadu, winning two bypolls held on Oct 6. Though Madurantakam and Dharapuram presented different political terrains, the ruling party won both seats by fielding former AIADMK MLAs Maragatham Kumaravel and P Sathyabama, who switched sides barely 20 days after the April 23 Assembly election.Sathyabama won Dharapuram by a margin of 9,471 votes, while Maragatham secured Madurantakam by 20,040 votes. DMK, which finished third in both constituencies in April, moved up to the second place, while AIADMK, which had won both seats in the April assembly election, slipped to third.The results increased TVK’s strength in the 234-member Assembly from 107 to 109. The victories could give the three-year-old party greater confidence as it prepares for bypolls in five other constituencies. However, the extent to which the ruling party can convert its alliance support into additional votes remains a question.The twin victories did not come without an intensive campaign. The Oct 6 bypolls prompted the 51-year-old actor-turned-politician to step up his efforts, from driving a bullock cart and a tractor to sipping tea at a roadside shop with locals and plucking drumsticks, as he campaigned for his party candidates.In Madurantakam, Maragatham built a lead from the first round of counting and widened it in successive rounds, finishing with 74,048 votes. She defeated DMK candidate I Paranthaman, who secured 54,008 votes, by 20,040 votes. Maragatham, who won the seat as an AIADMK candidate in April with 69,284 votes, increased her tally by 4,764 after switching to TVK. Her winning margin rose from 7,194 votes in April to 20,040 in October.Her victory was driven largely by the decline in support for her rivals. The DMK’s tally fell from 59,838 to 54,008, while AIADMK’s votes dropped from 69,284 to 47,450. The figures point to an erosion in support for both principal rivals, particularly AIADMK, which lost the seat after its former MLA switched to TVK.The result, therefore, presents a mixed picture for TVK. While Maragatham retained the seat under a different party banner and widened her winning margin, the modest increase in her vote count raises questions about the extent to which the ruling party’s status and its alliance with Congress, VCK, MDMK and IUML translated into additional votes.TVK leaders, including Aadhav Arjuna, had projected a victory margin of one lakh votes. The final tally fell well short of that claim, even as alliance leaders campaigned together in Madurantakam for the first time. VCK leader Thol Thirumavalavan had also urged his party’s supporters and cadres to work for Maragatham’s victory to ensure the continuation of the coalition govt.In Dharapuram, P Sathyabama won bypoll with a margin of around 9,471 votes, down from 16,727 votes in the April 23 Assembly election, when she contested on AIADMK’s two leaves symbol. The reduced margin indicates a tighter contest despite her retaining the seat under a new party banner.The results have consolidated TVK’s assembly position. articles.title: Hurricane Isaias approaches US Gulf Coast, raising storm surge fears
articles.summary: Hurricane Isaias intensified on Thursday as it moved towards the US Gulf Coast, prompting mandatory evacuations in parts of Florida.
articles.body: Hurricane Isaias intensified on Thursday as it moved towards the US Gulf Coast, prompting mandatory evacuations in parts of Florida. Forecasters warned of life-threatening storm surges, tornadoes and flooding, as authorities declared a state of emergency in affected areas.Storm Disrupts Oil and Gas ProductionHurricane Isaias has severely disrupted oil and gas production in the Gulf of Mexico, forcing energy companies to evacuate offshore platforms and suspend operations.The Marine Minerals Administration, which monitors offshore oil and gas operators in the Gulf of Mexico, said on Thursday that personnel had been evacuated from 121 production platforms. Five rigs were also reported to be outside dynamically positioned operations ahead of the storm.Around 1.3 million barrels of oil per day had been taken offline, accounting for approximately 63% of the Gulf’s current oil production. In addition, more than 1.1 billion cubic feet of natural gas per day had been shut off, representing around 57% of the region’s total output.It is stated that 16% of natural gas output and 25% of oil production had been shut in.According to a model forecast from consulting firm Earth Science Associates, around 9 million barrels of oil output might be lost in the Gulf throughout the storm's duration, a significant increase from the 7.1 million barrels affected by Tropical Storm Bertha in July.According to the Eartjh Science model, BP, Chevron, ENI, Murphy Oil, and She;ll are the companies that are most affected with this storm.Hurricane warnings and storm surge risksHurricane warnings were in effect from coastal Mississippi through Alabama to Florida’s Panhandle, while southeastern Louisiana was under tropical-storm and storm-surge warnings, according to the National Hurricane Center (NHC).Forecasters cautioned that storm surges could raise water levels by 5 to 7 feet (1.5 to 2.1 metres) above sea level in the worst-hit coastal areas. Rainfall totals were expected to reach 3 to 7 inches (8 to 18 cm), with isolated areas potentially receiving up to 15 inches (38 cm).The hurricane was expected to lose some strength as it neared the coast. However, increasing vertical wind shear, which can disrupt a storm’s circulation, was forecast to limit its intensity near landfall rather than eliminate the danger.Coastal communities prepare for evacuationsIn Florida, mandatory evacuations were ordered from noon local time on Thursday for coastal areas of Okaloosa County.Authorities urged tourists to leave the area and announced plans to shut three airports on Thursday evening. Earlier in the week, Governor Ron DeSantis had declared a state of emergency across 25 counties.Alabama Governor Kay Ivey declared a state of emergency covering 40 counties. Officials on Dauphin Island also issued an evacuation notice for the western part of the barrier island, effective Thursday evening.In Baldwin County, authorities encouraged residents in low-lying coastal areas to evacuate voluntarily and made preparations to open emergency shelters.Meanwhile, Jackson County and the city of Gautier in Mississippi declared local emergencies as coastal communities braced for possible flooding and power outages.You use AI every day. articles.title: ‘POSH is not a Chinese act’: Sacked JNU professor Angomcha Bimol Akoijam alleges 'witch hunt', demands evidence
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Congress MP Angomcha Bimol Akoijam, dismissed by Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) following an inquiry into sexual harassment allegations
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Congress MP Angomcha Bimol Akoijam, dismissed by Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) following an inquiry into sexual harassment allegations levelled against him by 11 students, has described the development as a “blessing in disguise”, alleging that it would expose what he called a “witch hunt”.In his first response to the dismissal, Akoijam said he had not received the inquiry report or the dismissal order and demanded that the evidence against him be made public.“I don't want to respond to social media. If this (incident) is true, it is a blessing in disguise for me, as I wanted these people to come out without their masks,” he said.“The POSH Act, 2013, is not a Chinese Act; it is an Indian law passed by the Indian Parliament. Let the countrymen see its requirements,” he added.Akoijam also said he had nothing to hide and called for the allegations and supporting evidence to be presented to him.“For me, this is the best thing that could happen to expose this 'witch hunt'. I have nothing to hide, even if it is true. I don't have the report or the dismissal order. I may look Chinese but I am an Indian and the Indian law should apply to me. If there are allegations then show me the evidence in the report or anywhere. Only then will you understand how this witch hunt has been going on. If it is true, let me see it,” he said.Why was Akoijam dismissed by JNU?JNU dismissed Akoijam, a professor at the Centre for the Study of Social Systems, with immediate effect on Friday after considering the findings of its Internal Committee (IC), which recommended a major penalty under the Central Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 1965.The dismissal order, signed by vice-chancellor Santishree D Pandit, said the decision was taken after following due process and considering the committee's report.The complaints against Akoijam were submitted on May 18. TOI first reported the complaints on September 6.Official sources said there was a disagreement within the inquiry committee over the recommended penalty. While the presiding officer and other members favoured a major penalty, student representatives reportedly supported a lesser punishment. The report was submitted with dissent after consultations with lawyers, sources said.Allegations against AkoijamThe allegations reportedly came to light after a student shared her account of an alleged interaction during a viva examination in a students-only WhatsApp group. Other students subsequently came forward with similar complaints.The complaints reportedly included allegations of sexually suggestive remarks during vivas and classes, inappropriate advances at gatherings at the professor's on-campus residence, and offers of higher marks in exchange for sexual favours.Akoijam is a Congress MP from the Inner Manipur constituency in Manipur and specialises in social and political psychology and cultural studies at JNU.(With inputs from PTI)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: In 2010, George Michael anonymously paid for Jo Maidment's IVF after seeing her on TV; two years later, she gave birth to Betsy and a bouquet of flowers finally revealed who had helped her
articles.summary: In 2010, British singer George Michael secretly paid for a woman's fertility treatment after watching her discuss her struggle to conceive on television.
articles.body: In 2010, British singer George Michael secretly paid for a woman's fertility treatment after watching her discuss her struggle to conceive on television. Jo Maidment had been denied NHS-funded treatment because her partner already had a child. Moved by her story, Michael offered to pay for a round of in vitro fertilisation (IVF) without revealing his identity. Two years later, Maidment gave birth to her daughter, Betsy.Maidment had appeared on ITV's This Morning to discuss her difficulties starting a family. According to ITV, she wanted to raise awareness about others facing similar problems, but two days after returning home, she received an unexpected call. A personal assistant told her that an unnamed businessman wanted to fund one cycle of IVF.Initially unsure about accepting the offer, Maidment eventually agreed. Her first IVF attempt was unsuccessful, but she had frozen eggs remaining from the treatment. A second attempt led to the birth of Betsy in 2012.It was only after bringing her daughter home that Maidment discovered who had paid for her treatment. A bouquet of flowers arrived with a card signed by George Michael, revealing that he had been the anonymous donor.Why George Michael paid for the treatmentMaidment had been refused NHS funding because her partner already had a daughter. After hearing her story on television, Michael arranged for his personal assistant, Michelle, to contact her.Recalling the call during a January 2017 appearance on This Morning, Maidment told presenters Phillip Schofield and Davina McCall, "I was home for two days and got a phone call from a PA saying a businessman would like to donate some money for one cycle of IVF for you."She admitted that she initially struggled to believe the offer and took several days to respond. "I didn’t believe it at first. And it took me a good few days to respond because that wasn’t what I came on the show for, I wanted to help other people in my position."But then we agreed to it, because the PA Michelle said it was what this particular man wanted.” Michael's identity remained a secret throughout her treatment.How a bouquet revealed George Michael's identityMaidment's first IVF cycle failed, but she was able to try again using eggs frozen during the process. The second attempt was successful, and she welcomed Betsy in 2012.A few days after returning home with her daughter, Maidment received several congratulatory cards and flowers. One particularly large bouquet came with a message that revealed who had helped her.She recalled, “It was a couple of days after we came home with Betsy and we had loads of cards and flowers. There was a massive bouquet of flowers that came and I read the card that said, ‘Congratulations to you both. Lots of love to Betsy. Love from Michelleand George Michael (AKA Anonymous) xx.'"Me and my husband read it hundreds of times to believe it.” The couple finally knew that the singer had funded the treatment that helped them become parents.Maidment shared the story after Michael's deathGeorge Michael died on Christmas Day in 2016, aged 53. Following his death, several stories emerged about donations he had made privately to individuals and charities.On January 3, 2017, Maidment returned to This Morning to reveal his role in helping her have Betsy. ITV said the disclosure was made with his family's blessing. "I cannot ever thank him enough for what he has done for me and my husband," she said.Maidment also expressed regret that she would never be able to thank Michael personally or introduce him to her daughter."Betsy is now four and a half. I was really upset when I found out George Michael had died because I can never thank him personally and he never got to meet her. Betsy will know when she’s old enough,” she said.According to ITV News, Maidment also donated her appearance fee from the programme to Childline.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Hours after Navi Pillay wins Nobel Peace prize, Trump hits ICC with major sanctions
articles.summary: The Donald Trump administration imposed sanctions on the International Criminal Court (ICC) on Friday, hours after former court judge Navi Pillay won the
articles.body: The Donald Trump administration imposed sanctions on the International Criminal Court (ICC) on Friday, hours after former court judge Navi Pillay won the Nobel Peace Prize for her efforts to promote international law.US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the sanctions were aimed at preventing the ICC from prosecuting American citizens. The move marks a significant escalation of the administration’s campaign against the Hague-based court.“President Trump will never allow the International Criminal Court to prosecute Americans,” Rubio said in a statement reviewed by Reuters ahead of the official announcement. “That is why, today, the United States is sanctioning the International Criminal Court. We will ban transactions with this rogue court, cutting off their resources and crippling its ability to operate.”The Trump administration has repeatedly criticised the ICC over its arrest warrants for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and former defence minister Yoav Gallant, as well as its earlier investigation into alleged crimes by US troops in Afghanistan, which the court has since closed.Washington has previously imposed sanctions on ICC prosecutors and judges, including its president, Tomoko Akane, and senior trial lawyer Abdoulaye Seye. The latest move targets the institution itself, raising concerns about its ability to operate and pursue cases involving alleged war crimes, genocide and crimes against humanity.The sanctions could further strain ties with European allies, many of whose countries are members of the ICC. The court, established in 2002, has 125 member states, including all European Union countries and most NATO members. The United States and Turkey are not members.Pillay, 85, a South African-born jurist and former United Nations human rights chief, won the Nobel Peace Prize for her work promoting international law. She previously served as an ICC judge from 2003 to 2008 and chaired a UN commission that concluded Israel had committed genocide in Gaza, a finding that Israel has strongly rejected.Announcing the award in Oslo, Norwegian Nobel Committee chairman Jørgen Watne Frydnes said the prize sought to remind the world that the rule of law underpins efforts to maintain peace and resolve conflicts without violence.Pillay, speaking after learning of the award in Nuremberg, Germany, warned that efforts to weaken international criminal justice threatened decades of progress.“(They) endanger the progress painstakingly made since Nuremberg, and they risk returning us to a world in which power, rather than law, determines whose suffering matters,” she said.You use AI every day. articles.body: Lok Sabha leader of opposition leader Rahul Gandhi on Friday said the opposition's protests against the Election Commission of India (ECI) had exposed a deeper problem with the government, asserting that sustained pressure over the next few days could bring it down.Addressing INDIA bloc MPs at the Central Hall of Samvidhan Sadan, Gandhi said the issue went beyond Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and called for the termination of the current government."There is a much deeper problem than Gyanesh Kumar and it requires termination of this current government," Congress leader Rahul Gandhi was quoted as saying by news agency PTI.He described the fight as one worth risking one's life for and accused Kumar of refusing to meet elected representatives."This is something that is worth fighting for and dying for," Gandhi said.The Congress leader also said the Chief Election Commissioner was merely a service provider and criticised him for saying he would not meet elected representatives."If we continue to push the way we have in last three-four days, I guarantee this government will fall," the former Congress chief said.Gandhi also invoked Jawaharlal Nehru's historic address delivered from the Central Hall of Parliament on August 14, 1947, as the INDIA bloc intensified its campaign against the Election Commission."Jawaharlal Nehru gave a very famous speech. It was given from the Central Hall of Parliament on 14 August 1947. I want to quote a little bit from it. It is a fateful moment for us in India, for all Asia and for the world. A new star rises, the star of freedom in the East, a new hope comes into being, a vision long cherished materialises. May the star never set and that hope never be betrayed..." Rahul Gandhi said.The address came amid a political dispute over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and allegations of bias against the poll body.The INDIA bloc and the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) have alleged large-scale voter disenfranchisement, claiming that more than 13 crore names were deleted during the draft-roll stage of the revision to target citizens opposed to the ruling BJP.The controversy intensified following reports that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised internal objections over voter additions, deletions and administrative anomalies in the electoral software.The Election Commission rejected allegations of an institutional breakdown, saying 13.39 crore electors had been flagged under the standard ASD categories of Absent, Shifted, Dead and duplicate. articles.title: In 2006, George W Bush used a presidential proclamation to establish a 139,797-square-mile marine monument in the Northwestern Hawaiian Islands; it later became the foundation for much larger protected seascape
articles.summary: In 2006, President George W. Bush used a presidential proclamation to establish the Northwestern Hawaiian Islands Marine National Monument, protecting 139,797 square miles of ocean and reinforcing the conservation of this vital marine ecosystem. Discover the impact and expansion of this monumental decision.
articles.body: Far from Hawaii’s main islands lies a chain of atolls, coral reefs, submerged banks and islands spread across a vast stretch of the Pacific. Much of the region is remote enough that its reefs and wildlife developed with relatively little human interference. In 2006, the US government took unprecedented large action to preserve that marine environment, using a presidential proclamation rather than waiting for Congress to pass new legislation.According to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), on 15 June 2006, President George W. Bush established the Northwestern Hawaiian Islands Marine National Monument under the Antiquities Act. The monument covered 139,797 square miles (362,073 sq km) of ocean, islands, reefs, shoals and surrounding waters. At the time, it was among the world's largest marine protected areas. The region supported more than 7,000 marine species, with roughly a quarter found only in the Hawaiian Archipelago.A vast ocean protection zoneThe designation also marked a major departure from how protected areas were typically created. Instead of designating a traditional land-based national monument, the administration used the Antiquities Act of 1906 to designate a vast area of oceans and their lands. This act gives U.S. presidents the power to declare national monuments on federal lands that contain historical or scientific objects.According to the George W. Bush White House Archives, the proclamation placed the waters and federal lands within the monument under a broader conservation framework. Federal lands and interests were withdrawn from activities such as mining and mineral leasing, while restrictions were placed on activities that could damage the marine ecosystem. The area was important not simply because of its size, but because it contained coral reefs, fish, seabirds, marine mammals and other wildlife, including the endangered Hawaiian monk seal and threatened green sea turtle. The proclamation also recognised the region's cultural importance to Native Hawaiians and its connections to early Polynesian history.Fishing and other activities faced restrictionsProtecting an area this large inevitably meant changes to activities within the monument. The proclamation prohibited unauthorised entry, recreational and commercial activities, resource extraction and waste dumping. Commercial fishing was also phased out over five years. However, the regulations were not intended to sever all ties between people and the region. The proclamation made provisions for Native Hawaiians to access the region for cultural purposes through a permit process.It also provided for a management system that involved NOAA, the US Fish and Wildlife Service and the State of Hawaii. While NOAA had the lead role in managing the marine areas, the Fish and Wildlife Service managed areas that were part of wildlife refuges and the Battle of Midway National Memorial. This management system was critical because the monument encompassed both marine and terrestrial regions.From Northwestern Hawaiian Islands to PapahānaumokuākeaIn March 2007, Bush amended the original proclamation and gave it the name Papahānaumokuākea Marine National Monument, recognising its Native Hawaiian cultural significance. As reported by Papahānaumokuākea, the monument's story did not end with its designation. A decade later, in August 2016, President Barack Obama expanded the monument by another 442,781 square miles, bringing its total area to 582,578 square miles.Today, Papahānaumokuākea is managed jointly by federal agencies, the State of Hawaii and the Office of Hawaiian Affairs, safeguarding reefs, islands and surrounding waters that support thousands of marine species while also protecting an area of major cultural importance to Native Hawaiians. President Bush's 2006 designation was not just about protecting remote Hawaiian islands. This move created a conservation model covering almost 140,000 square miles of ocean and laid the groundwork for future expansions.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: At 73, California cyclist Mark Strauss rode 3,200 miles from the Pacific to the Atlantic over 69 days to fight childhood hunger; his No Kid Hungry campaign has now raised $740,000 toward a $1 million goal
articles.summary: At 73, Mark Strauss set himself a daunting challenge: cycle 3,200 miles from the Pacific to the Atlantic and raise $1 million for children facing hunger.
articles.body: At 73, Mark Strauss set himself a daunting challenge: cycle 3,200 miles from the Pacific to the Atlantic and raise $1 million for children facing hunger. The California cyclist completed the journey in 69 days, travelling across the country while meeting people who supported his cause along the way. His ride has now raised $740,000 for No Kid Hungry, leaving $260,000 to reach the campaign’s goal, according to the ride’s official website. Strauss’s journey was not simply about distance or endurance. As No Kid Hungry’s account of the ride explains, he was motivated by the reality that millions of children in the United States struggle to access food. For him, the cause was simple: children need food to learn, grow and reach their potential.Turning concern into a cross-country rideStrauss began planning the ride after learning that 14 million children in the United States face hunger. He described the figure as “unacceptable,” especially in a country with abundant resources and opportunities, according to No Kid Hungry’s account of his campaign.Cycling offered a way to bring together two things that mattered to him: a personal passion and a practical effort to help. Strauss explored organisations working on food insecurity and eventually connected with No Kid Hungry. The organisation’s work with schools, food banks and community partners gave him a way to turn a long-distance ride into fundraising for programmes that support children.The challenge was substantial. Over 69 days, Strauss travelled 3,200 miles from the Pacific coast to the Atlantic, crossing varied landscapes and weather conditions. The ride demanded more than physical stamina. It required daily preparation, route planning and the persistence to keep going when the road was tiring or unexpected obstacles arose.Help along the roadThe journey also became a story about the people Strauss met. In a blog post, he said it was difficult to choose a single favourite moment from the ride because the changing scenery, rivers, mountains and conversations with locals all became part of the experience.One encounter in Ohio stayed with him. A construction site blocked the route, and getting around it would have meant a long detour. Workers stepped in to help, moving equipment so Strauss and his team could pass through safely. After hearing about the purpose of the ride, the crew made time to clear a path.The moment was small in practical terms, but it captured the generosity he encountered repeatedly. People offered donations, food, encouragement and help with the journey. Strauss said supporters came from different backgrounds and viewpoints, united by a willingness to help children.That support did not remove the difficulty of cycling thousands of miles. But it gave the trip a human dimension: the campaign was not only one cyclist pushing through each day, but also a succession of people deciding that the cause was worth supporting.Seeing the work up closeAlong the route, Strauss visited community partners working with No Kid Hungry, including food banks and school districts. These visits allowed him to see how local organisations help children access meals and how donations can support programmes on the ground.The No Kid Hungry website says the organisation works with schools, food banks and community groups to connect children with food. Its campaign page also describes school and summer meal programmes as part of the wider effort to address hunger when school is out.For Strauss, these visits brought the cause into sharper focus. The need was not an abstract figure or a fundraising message. It was visible in communities where families, teachers and food programmes were working to make sure children had something to eat.He reflected on the contrast between finishing the ride and the persistence of the problem. Once the 69 days were over, there was no bicycle to prepare or route to study, but children still woke up hungry and families still faced difficulty putting meals on the table.$740,000 raised, $260,000 to goThe ride’s official website reports that the campaign has raised $740,000 toward its $1 million target. That leaves $260,000 to go. The site says the funds will help No Kid Hungry continue supporting efforts to provide meals to children across the country.The campaign’s figure has increased since No Kid Hungry published its blog about the ride. At that point, the organisation reported that Strauss had raised $720,000 and was seeking the remaining $280,000. The current campaign page now places the total at $740,000.The organisation says donations help support school and summer meal programmes and other efforts to connect children with food. Its website notes that a donation of $1 can help provide 10 meals for children, though the exact impact of contributions depends on how funds are used across programmes.The remaining distance to the fundraising goal may be much smaller than the 3,200 miles Strauss already covered, but it still represents an important final stretch. His physical ride is complete; the effort to raise support for the cause continues.A ride that keeps goingWhen Strauss returned home, the daily routine of the ride ended. There were no more mileage targets, route checks or support vehicles waiting nearby. But the reason he set out remained: children across the country continue to need dependable access to food.That is why the campaign’s progress matters beyond the cyclist’s personal achievement. The 3,200-mile journey helped draw attention to childhood hunger and directed donations towards an organisation already working with local partners. Its impact will be measured not only in miles or dollars, but in the meals and support those resources help make possible.Strauss’s ride began with a clear belief that food is fundamental to a child’s ability to learn and grow. At 73, he turned that belief into a cross-country effort, one day and one mile at a time. With $740,000 raised and $260,000 still needed to reach the goal, the campaign’s final chapter is being written by the supporters who continue to join him.You use AI every day. articles.title: Trump sets up committee to probe Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook in latest bid to fire her
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump has set up a committee to investigate Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook over allegations that she made false statements in
articles.body: US President Donald Trump has set up a committee to investigate Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook over allegations that she made false statements in mortgage applications, renewing his efforts to remove her from the central bank.The committee will examine the allegations and report to Trump on whether there is sufficient cause to remove Cook, according to a presidential memorandum published on the White House website. The panel will hold an in-person hearing at the White House on November 5, where Cook is expected to respond to the charges. The hearing will not be public, but a transcript will be published, the memo said.Trump’s latest move comes after the US Supreme Court allowed Cook to remain in her position following his earlier attempt to fire her in August 2025. The court’s June ruling said the president could pursue her removal again if he provided adequate notice and an opportunity for her to respond to the allegations.Trump initially sought to remove Cook after accusing her of mortgage fraud over applications filed in 2021 that allegedly listed two different properties as her primary residence. Mortgages for primary residences can come with lower interest rates or other favourable terms.Cook has denied wrongdoing and has not been charged with a crime. Her lawyers, Abbe Lowell and Norman Eisen, have described the alleged discrepancy as an inadvertent error, arguing that it does not amount to fraud.In a statement, the lawyers said Cook welcomed the opportunity to present the facts and clear her name. They added that they were in discussions with the White House to determine whether the proposed process would provide a genuine opportunity to respond to the allegations.Trump said in the memorandum that he was responsible for ensuring that the law was faithfully executed, including by removing officials he believed could not be trusted to tell the truth and follow the law.The case has raised concerns about the independence of the Federal Reserve, which sets US monetary policy. Trump has repeatedly called for interest rate cuts, while criticising the central bank’s rate decisions.Cook’s position on the Fed’s seven-member board of governors also makes her one of the 12 voting members of the Federal Open Market Committee, which determines the benchmark interest rate.Cook was appointed to the Fed board by former President Joe Biden in 2022 and reappointed in 2023. Her current term runs until 2038. She was the first Black woman to serve on the central bank’s board.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A wind-tunnel experiment paired two vertical-axis turbines; closely spaced counter-rotating models produced 13% to 16% more power than two isolated turbines
articles.summary: Discover how a groundbreaking wind tunnel experiment revealed the potential for vertical-axis turbines to outperform traditional setups by generating up to 16% more power when paired closely together. This research challenges conventional wind farm designs and could reshape the future of wind energy production.
articles.body: One basic criterion governing wind farms is that each turbine needs room. Developers disperse the industry's well-known three-bladed machines widely to prevent one from starving the next of wind since they leave a long, turbulent wake behind them. That configuration has never been suitable for vertical-axis turbines, the upright type that spins somewhat like an egg whisk. A single one typically gathers less energy than a traditional design, which contributes to the problem.Some researchers have explored the opposite approach: placing vertical-axis turbines close together. A 2004 US patent described a coupled vertical-axis turbine with two counter-rotating rotors, while Caltech researcher John Dabiri later proposed arranging counter-rotating vertical-axis turbines in close proximity, inspired in part by fish schooling. A 2021 paper by Yoshifumi Jodai of Kagawa National Institute of Technology and Yutaka Hara of Tottori University cited Dabiri’s work estimating that a vertical-axis wind farm could achieve six to nine times the power density of modern horizontal-axis wind farms.One of the clearest answers so far came from a wind tunnel study published in February 2020 that tested the hypothesis on genuine spinning models. Two small turbines placed close together produced a higher combined power coefficient than two identical turbines operating separately. What follows discusses how the experiment worked and how big the gain was and why it matters for wind generation.How the test workedAntoine Vergaerde led the 2020 study, with researchers from Vrije Universiteit Brussel and collaborators from other institutions. Each turbine had a two-bladed H-type Darrieus design, i.e., two straight blades maintained parallel to the shaft by struts. The blades were symmetrical with an NACA 0018 aerofoil shape. The solidity, that is, the fraction of the swept area occupied by the blades, was 0.20.The researchers measured the mechanical power output of an individual turbine and then compared it with the output of two turbines operating as a closely spaced, counter-rotating pair. The rotors in the paired runs spun in opposite directions, rather like meshing gears, and sat extremely close together. The distance between their shafts was only 1.2 to 1.3 times the width of one rotor. They tried it both ways, one with the blades facing each other going with the wind and the other with them going against the wind. They compared the power coefficient, a measure of how much of the wind’s energy is caught, to see if two turbines together were better than two on their own.What did the figures showThe 2020 Renewable Energy paper found average relative increases of 13% to 16% in the paired turbines’ power coefficient compared with two isolated turbines. At the smallest spacings tried, the improvement was as much as nearly 16 per cent. The experiment was set up to verify what computer simulations had indicated, and the measured gains were consistent with those predictions.Earlier numerical work by Zanforlin and Nishino helped explain the aerodynamic mechanism: the two closely spaced rotors alter the incoming flow between them, improving the conditions for lift and torque.Not every lab has named the same winner. The best practical spacing in the Japanese test, which used small 3D-printed rotors just 50 millimetres across, was a gap of barely a fifth of a rotor width. The authors attribute such differences to rotor solidity, which is a reminder that the outcomes are dependent on the exact turbine design.From tunnel to wind parkScaling up brings new questions. Real farms are exposed to turbulent wind and a high number of turbines, and the wakes of vertical axis machines behave differently than those of ordinary rotors. The architecture is so important, as field trials of offshore farms with conventional turbines have shown wake losses in the range of 10-23 per cent depending on spacing and wind.In 2025, researchers from Delft University of Technology and their collaborators published a wind-tunnel experiment involving nine H-type vertical-axis turbines arranged in a 3×3 grid in Wind Energy Science. They used fixed blade-pitch settings to alter wake interactions within the simulated farm. The researchers calculated that the available power within the simulated farm could increase by factors of 6.4 and 2.1 for the two blade-pitch settings, respectively, when potential downstream rotors were directly aligned with upstream ones, compared with the baseline case. Those numbers are for wind energy accessible in the wake, not electricity transmitted to a grid, so they indicate potential, not demonstrated output.The 2020 experiment found that closely spaced counter-rotating H-type turbines could achieve a 13% to 16% increase in power coefficient compared with two isolated turbines. Spacing, rotation direction and rotor design all affected the result, while wind-tunnel tests alone cannot establish how a large commercial farm would perform. The findings nevertheless support further investigation of high-density vertical-axis turbine layouts.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: INDIA bloc leaders on Friday met President Droupadi Murmu and submitted a memorandum outlining four demands, as the opposition intensified its campaign against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.In the memorandum submitted to the President, the opposition demanded: CEC’s resignation, scrapping of assembly elections held over the last two years, suspension of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and a return to paper ballots.“We urge you to take cognisance of this grave situation and use your good offices to ensure that the following demands are addressed without delay,” the memorandum read, listing four demands, including the restoration of 13.30 crore voters allegedly deleted from electoral rolls.The memorandum added: “We approach you because, in moments when every other door has been closed, the people of India look to the Office of the President as the final guardian of that covenant...”After meeting Murmu, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi said he had expected the President to deny that vote theft was taking place but was surprised by her response.“I expected President to deny that 'vote chori' is taking place; I was shocked, stunned that she accepted what we said,” Rahul said.He also announced that opposition leaders would approach the Supreme Court on Monday. “We will go to Supreme Court on Monday to meet Chief Justice of India and hand over memorandum to him,” he said.The delegation included Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Former West Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee, Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah and leaders from other INDIA bloc parties.Earlier, Opposition MPs marched from Parliament House towards Vijay Chowk carrying a “Save Democracy” banner but were stopped by police barricades.The latest action follows several days of protests against Gyanesh Kumar.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Queen Elizabeth helped save rare horse breeds from extinction; she bought a Cleveland Bay colt destined for export when only six purebred stallions remained
articles.summary: Six purebred Cleveland Bay stallions.
articles.body: Six purebred Cleveland Bay stallions. That was all that remained of the breed in 1960, and the reigning monarch soon stepped in to buy a young colt destined for export. Queen Elizabeth II bred horses in her private stables and in the working yards that supplied royal and state occasions, and the breeds she championed included Highland ponies, Fell ponies and Cleveland Bays. Her grandfather also bred Cleveland Bays, and her Balmoral prefix for Fell ponies, begun in 1952, kept registering foals into 2021. Conservation groups still credit her yards with keeping bloodlines alive through mechanisation, crossbreeding and shrinking demand.Peggy the Shetland pony and the childhood gift that began her life of horse breeding in royal yardsThe Royal Family's official website traces the Queen's horsemanship to a Shetland pony named Peggy, a gift from her grandfather, King George V. From that first pony, she grew into a rider, owner and breeder the website calls hugely knowledgeable. Her passion was visible at the Derby at Epsom and Royal Ascot, and her runners won, Landau took the Rous Memorial Stakes in 1954, Estimate won the Gold Cup at Royal Ascot in 2013, and Highclere took the Prix de Diane at Chantilly in 1975. Racing was only one side of her stables. According to the same page, she also helped ensure the survival of several rare horse and pony breeds through breeding programmes in her private yards and in the working yards that produced horses for royal and state occasions.How a colt saved from export rescued a near-lost horse breedIn 1960, only six purebred Cleveland Bay stallions were alive, according to The Livestock Conservancy, a nonprofit organisation working to protect more than 150 heritage farm animal breeds. It explains that the breed was developed in Yorkshire for strength, speed, soundness and stamina, but mechanisation ended demand for farm, coach and road horses, and breeders crossbred their mares because the lighter, faster crossbreds were worth more. The Queen, whose grandfather had also bred Cleveland Bays, bought a pure colt named Mulgrave Supreme, born in 1961 and earmarked for export, and used him as a stud. The Conservancy still lists the breed as critically endangered, though perhaps as many as one thousand horses are alive today, about 180 of them purebreds in North America.Highland, Fell and Cleveland Bay breeds: how the private and working royal yards helped them surviveThe royal website states that the Queen was involved in ensuring the survival of a number of rare breeds of horses and ponies through breeding programmes, and it names where those programmes ran, her private yards, and the working yards that produced horses for Royal and State occasions. Horses from the working yards had a public job, serving those occasions. The website names the breeds she championed as Highland ponies, Fell ponies and Cleveland Bays. It does not give foal numbers, dates or the names of individual animals, so the account stays at the level of a stated commitment rather than a record of results, but the three breeds named are clear and specific.Highland ponies and Old Spots pigs: Royal herds beyond the horse stablesHighland ponies were bred to haul timber and game and plough small Scottish farms, and the Queen kept a large working stud of them; the royal family's website lists them among the breeds she championed. Her farm animals followed the same pattern. On her Gloucestershire estate, the Queen also raised Gloucester Old Spots pigs, a docile, intelligent breed that nearly vanished in the 1960s and has slowly increased since.Riding well into her outdoor life shared with horses and dogsShe rode well into her nineties and took great pleasure in walking in the countryside and spending time with her dogs. The page lists riding first, ahead of walking and her dogs. The timeline is what stands out, a Shetland pony received from her grandfather in childhood, and riding still part of her life in her nineties. The page does not say which horses she rode in later years, so it would be wrong to link her riding to any one of the breeds she championed. What it does show is that her involvement with horses was practical and physical, not limited to owning racehorses or attending meetings.King Charles the Third, the Rare Breeds Survival Trust and the Sandringham Estate continue her workKing Charles the Third now carries the family's involvement forward. The Livestock Conservancy notes that he is patron of the Rare Breeds Survival Trust, its sister organisation in the United Kingdom, and is converting the Queen's Sandringham Estate to organic farming, a system he says works with nature rather than against it. The Conservancy still classifies the Cleveland Bay, Fell and Highland as critically endangered, so their survival depends on breeders, registries and owners.You use AI every day.
